applied.problem: Three absolutes: the notes say low resistance is 'generally' under 1 Ω; crossed phases give a short only where the cable closes onto another supply (otherwise reversed rotation); and 'whatever is wrong with L2' presumes a fault the passing test has not shown.

'A sound core at 12 °C reads 3.14% low' holds only for a core exactly on its certificate (a sound core can sit anywhere within 2%); and the 2.40 km is the practice case's length, unlabelled in a sentence read alone.

Safety order: the notes clamp on before removing the earths, so an unearthed core with induced voltage is never handled; and P probes on the core beyond the C clamps see no current there, so it is P on the clamps, not 'outside', that adds contact resistance.

With the P probes on the core outside the C clamps no current flows between P and C, so the clamps' contact resistance does not join; it joins when the P probes are clipped on the C clamps, as the lesson's own picture shows.
Only a core exactly on its 20 °C certificate reads 3.14% low at 12 °C; a sound core can sit anywhere within 2% of it.

notes.problem: String B's loops (339.31 mΩ etc.) are given to 0.01 mΩ, but the DLRO10HD's 2.5 Ω ranges resolve 0.1 mΩ at ±0.2% ±200 µΩ (about ±0.9 mΩ here), so L2's 0.72 mΩ gap and 'L1 and L3 match exactly' sit inside the meter's accuracy; a 10 mA 2.5 Ω green range also exists.
